statement: A community pool offers two ways to pay. With a season pass, a swimmer pays $\$84$ once plus a $\$1.50$ locker fee for each visit. Without a pass, a swimmer pays $\$6.75$ per visit, locker included. What is the least number of visits for which the season pass costs less than paying per visit?

choices.misconception: I forgot the locker fee that comes with the season pass and compared $84$ with $6.75v$, which gave $v > 12.4$, so I chose 13.
I solved $84 + 1.50v = 6.75v$ and got exactly 16, but at 16 visits the two options cost the same, so the pass is not yet cheaper.
I divided the $\$84$ pass price by the $\$1.50$ locker fee and got 56.

hints: Write an expression for the cost of each option after $v$ visits.
Set up $84 + 1.50v < 6.75v$ and solve for $v$. Remember that $v$ must be a whole number.
The inequality becomes $84 < 5.25v$, so $v > 16$. Which whole number is the smallest one greater than 16?

solutions.reliable: After $v$ visits the season pass costs $84 + 1.50v$ dollars and paying per visit costs $6.75v$ dollars. The pass is cheaper when $84 + 1.50v < 6.75v$, that is $84 < 5.25v$, so $v > 16$. At $16$ visits both options cost $\$108$, so the least whole number of visits is $17$. Check: at $17$ visits the pass costs $\$109.50$ and paying per visit costs $\$114.75$.
solutions.elegant: Each visit with the pass saves $6.75 - 1.50 = \$5.25$. The pass is cheaper once those savings exceed $\$84$, and $84 \div 5.25 = 16$ exactly, so the savings first exceed $\$84$ on visit $17$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
